    start mid-class. They are still never reformatted.

        self.config = config
        self._splitters: dict[str, RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter] = {}

    def _splitter_for(self, language: str) -> RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter:

answer: The `take_token` function implements a token bucket algorithm to rate limit requests. It allows a specified number of requests (`capacity`) within a given time period (`period_seconds`) per key. If the limit is not exceeded, it returns a `Decision` object indicating that the request is allowed. If the limit is exceeded, it returns a `Decision` object indicating that the request is not allowed and specifies how long the user should wait before retrying [1].

"""
CORS: lets a browser app served from another address (for example the Vite dev server on
http://localhost:5173) call this API.

A browser only lets a page read responses from ANOTHER origin when the API says so with CORS headers.
Without them every request from the frontend is blocked by the browser, even though the API is fine.

Choices made here:
  * Only the origins listed in CORS_ORIGINS are allowed (no "*"), so other websites cannot call the API
    from a user's browser.
  * No cookies: the frontend sends its Clerk token in the Authorization header, so credentials stay off.
  * Retry-After and X-RateLimit-* are EXPOSED. Browsers hide all non-standard response headers from
    JavaScript unless they are listed, and the frontend needs Retry-After to show "try again in N seconds".
  * An empty CORS_ORIGINS turns CORS off (the right setting when the frontend is served from the same origin).
"""

ALLOWED_METHODS = ["GET", "POST", "PATCH", "DELETE", "OPTIONS"]
ALLOWED_HEADERS = ["Authorization", "Content-Type"]
EXPOSED_HEADERS = ["Retry-After", "X-RateLimit-Limit", "X-RateLimit-Reset"]


def parse_origins(value: str) -> list[str]:
    """"http://a.com, http://b.com/" -> ["http://a.com", "http://b.com"] (browsers send origins without a trailing slash)."""
    return [origin.strip().rstrip("/") for origin in value.split(",") if origin.strip()]

    """Keyword arguments for Starlette's CORSMiddleware, or None when no origin is configured."""
    origins = parse_origins(cors_origins)
    if not origins:
        return None
    return {
        "allow_origins": origins,
        "allow_credentials": False,
        "allow_methods": ALLOWED_METHODS,
        "allow_headers": ALLOWED_HEADERS,
        "expose_headers": EXPOSED_HEADERS,
        "max_age": 600,                      # the browser may cache a preflight answer for 10 minutes
    }

   0:59 and N more at 1:01.

    text = error_message or ""

FAILURE_REASONS = (

    ("nothing left after cleaning", "No readable text was found in the file."),
    ("chunking gave no output", "No readable text was found in the file."),

    ("Failed after", "A temporary problem stopped processing this file. Please try uploading it again."),
    ("Failed to queue ingestion", "Processing could not be started. Please try uploading the file again."),
)
GENERIC_FAILURE = "Processing failed. Please try uploading the file again."


def friendly_failure_reason(status: str, error_message: str | None) -> str | None:
    """None unless the document failed (a retrying document may still carry an old error text)."""
    if status != "failed":
        return None
    text = error_message or ""
    for prefix, message in FAILURE_REASONS:
        if text.startswith(prefix):
            return message
    return GENERIC_FAILURE

        return friendly_failure_reason(self.status, self.error_message)

"""
CORS: lets a browser app served from another address (for example the Vite dev server on
http://localhost:5173) call this API.

A browser only lets a page read responses from ANOTHER origin when the API says so with CORS headers.
Without them every request from the frontend is blocked by the browser, even though the API is fine.

Choices made here:
  * Only the origins listed in CORS_ORIGINS are allowed (no "*"), so other websites cannot call the API
    from a user's browser.
  * No cookies: the frontend sends its Clerk token in the Authorization header, so credentials stay off.
  * Retry-After and X-RateLimit-* are EXPOSED. Browsers hide all non-standard response headers from
    JavaScript unless they are listed, and the frontend needs Retry-After to show "try again in N seconds".
  * An empty CORS_ORIGINS turns CORS off (the right setting when the frontend is served from the same origin).
"""

ALLOWED_METHODS = ["GET", "POST", "PATCH", "DELETE", "OPTIONS"]
ALLOWED_HEADERS = ["Authorization", "Content-Type"]
EXPOSED_HEADERS = ["Retry-After", "X-RateLimit-Limit", "X-RateLimit-Reset"]


def parse_origins(value: str) -> list[str]:
    """"http://a.com, http://b.com/" -> ["http://a.com", "http://b.com"] (browsers send origins without a trailing slash)."""
    return [origin.strip().rstrip("/") for origin in value.split(",") if origin.strip()]


def cors_options(cors_origins: str) -> dict | None:
    """Keyword arguments for Starlette's CORSMiddleware, or None when no origin is configured."""
    origins = parse_origins(cors_origins)
    if not origins:
        return None
    return {
        "allow_origins": origins,
        "allow_credentials": False,
        "allow_methods": ALLOWED_METHODS,
        "allow_headers": ALLOWED_HEADERS,
        "expose_headers": EXPOSED_HEADERS,
        "max_age": 600,                      # the browser may cache a preflight answer for 10 minutes
    }

"""
Rate limiting: protects the expensive parts of the API (/ask costs LLM time and, through the
Gemini fallback, free-tier quota; uploads cost embedding work) from one user, a bug or a script.

TWO ALGORITHMS, both keeping their state in Redis (so it survives restarts and is shared by every
server process, unlike a Python variable):

1. TOKEN BUCKET  ("10 questions per minute")
   A bucket holds up to `capacity` tokens. Every request takes one; an empty bucket means "no".
   Tokens flow back at a steady rate (capacity / period). Nothing runs on a timer: when a request
   arrives we work out how many tokens would have flowed back since the last visit:

       tokens = min(capacity, tokens + seconds_since_last_visit * refill_rate)

   It allows a short burst (up to `capacity`) and then smooths out, and it knows exactly how long a
   rejected caller must wait. A plain "N per minute" counter would let someone send N requests at
   0:59 and N more at 1:01.

2. FIXED-WINDOW COUNTER  ("100 questions per day")
   One counter per user per UTC day. At the limit, "no"; the key expires at the next UTC midnight, so
   it resets by itself. Its weakness (a burst around midnight can use two days' budget at once) does
   not matter for a safety net.

WHY LUA: "read the bucket, refill it, take a token, write it back" must happen as ONE step. Done from
Python in separate calls, two simultaneous requests could both see "1 token left" and both take it.
Redis runs a Lua script without interleaving anything else, and in a single network round trip.

FAIL OPEN: if Redis is down or slow the request is allowed (and a warning is logged). The limiter is
a safety net; it must never be the reason the API is unavailable.

"""

http://localhost:5173) call this API.

A browser only lets a page read responses from ANOTHER origin when the API says so with CORS headers.
Without them every request from the frontend is blocked by the browser, even though the API is fine.

  * Only the origins listed in CORS_ORIGINS are allowed (no "*"), so other websites cannot call the API
    from a user's browser.
  * No cookies: the frontend sends its Clerk token in the Authorization header, so credentials stay off.
  * Retry-After and X-RateLimit-* are EXPOSED. Browsers hide all non-standard response headers from
    JavaScript unless they are listed, and the frontend needs Retry-After to show "try again in N seconds".
  * An empty CORS_ORIGINS turns CORS off (the right setting when the frontend is served from the same origin).

ALLOWED_METHODS = ["GET", "POST", "PATCH", "DELETE", "OPTIONS"]
ALLOWED_HEADERS = ["Authorization", "Content-Type"]
EXPOSED_HEADERS = ["Retry-After", "X-RateLimit-Limit", "X-RateLimit-Reset"]


def parse_origins(value: str) -> list[str]:
    """"http://a.com, http://b.com/" -> ["http://a.com", "http://b.com"] (browsers send origins without a trailing slash)."""

    if not origins:

    splits on actual heading tags (h1/h2/h3) and attaches the heading
    hierarchy as metadata — meaningfully better than character
    splitting for markup with real structure.

    the recursive splitter to keep chunks under chunk_size.

            headers_to_split_on=list(config.html_headers_to_split_on)
        )

            encoding_name=config.encoding_name,

            chunk_overlap=config.chunk_overlap,
            separators=["\n\n", "\n", ". ", " ", ""],

        # be arbitrarily long.
        return self._size_splitter.split_documents(header_split_docs)
